<cite ref="Sotah 8b:5">Sot. 8ᵇ</cite> (prov.) <he>שליח ע׳ וסיים מסאני</he> stripped to nakedness, but shoes he has on (there is more disgrace in a disharmonious toilet than in a uniformly poor one); <cite ref="Ketubot 65b:1">Keth. 65ᵇ</cite> top (ref. to the disproportion between the obligatory outfit of garments and that of shoes, <cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 5:8">ib. V, 8</cite>) <he>האי תנא שליח ע׳ וכ׳</he> would that teacher have applied to her the proverb, stripped to nakedness &c.? Y. ib. VI, 30ᵈ <he>אורחא … הני לי מיקום ערטיליי וכ׳</he> it is usual for a man to say (to his father-in-law), I will rather go naked (deprive myself &c., v. <cite ref="P01326"><he>עָרוֹם</he></cite>), if only my wife be covered (but by saying this he does not mean to release him from the obligation of giving his daughter an appropriate outfit).
